sections.text_helper: Section 39.5.2 "Decimation" in chapter 39 (Digital camera interface pixel pipeline (DCMIPP)), RM0486 Rev 4, page 1841.
sections.section_content:
The decimation allows to cheaply downsize a frame.
Based on parallel interface camera module:
– Factor 1x, 2x, 4x at data/byte level depending on the configuration of bit field
BSM[1:0] of the DCMIPP_P0PPCR register. The decimation is not working directly
at pixel level, but it is based on either byte or 16-bit word granularity (for padded
raw 10, for instance) to make equivalent decimation to one pixel out of two. Bit
OEBS is used to start from the odd or even byte (or data) to capture first.
– The decimation can also be based on entire line, by capturing all the lines, or one
line out of two thanks to bit LSM. Here, again, choice is given to the software to
reject odd or even lines within the frame by configuring bit OELS.
When the camera sensor module is designed on CSI-2 interface, the decimation can be
based filter out potentially, one line out of two. Indeed, each packet is by protocol composed
for an entire line.
Note: Care must be taken when the CSI-2 header is dumped, as it is 32-bit wide, and it increases
by one unit the data counter, taking part of the decimation. It is advised not to use the CSI
header option when decimation takes place.
[Table 340. DCMIPP_P0PPCR bit function]
